findings.claim: 'Known-thin' over-counts unless the live parameter count is joined in. All 13 thin cop/ pages document node types carrying ZERO live parameter tuples - their documentation is complete for what the node is, and no floor requiring a described parameter can ever be cleared by a parameterless node. Copernicus therefore has NO documentation gap at this floor. The real gap is 10 pages in lop/ and cop2/, led by lop/usdrender_rop (166 live parameter tuples, no summary and no described parameter), cop2/rop_comp (73) and lop/usd_rop (51 - 36 described parameters but no authored summary). method_notes: R60 taken literally: four help pages were transcribed BY HAND from the archive before the parser was pointed at them - cop/chromakey (one of the new COPs, and CRLF), cop2/emboss (BOM, indent-4, #channels-only), lop/distantlight (title-first, 0 parameters raw and 87 resolved) and cop/adjacency_distort (#contentfrom with no inline prose). Those transcriptions are the ground truth, not parser output.

Two controls went red on first run and in BOTH cases the CONTROL was wrong, not the reader. Recorded inline at the control rather than quietly repaired: N7's mutation left nested entries in place so the fold pass rescued the page it was meant to strip; B3 expected one Vimeo id and the trap binds four.

The reader is one instrument and its per-context behaviour is DERIVED PER PAGE rather than switched on the context name - header order is measured (cop/ is 98% directives-first, lop/ 79% title-first) and item base indent is resolved per (section, heading) scope (cop/ at column 0, cop2/ at indent 4+). Switching on the context name would be right today and wrong on the next build.

Prior work was reused rather than re-derived where it was committed and calibrated: harness/notes/h9/helpdoc.py supplies the cross-zip corpus loader, the utf-8-sig decode, the loose-directory load and the anchored-block machinery. Three behaviours it lacks were added here (@section anchors, #contentfrom, menu folding) rather than patched into a committed module another leg depends on.

The doc axis and the runtime axis are produced by SEPARATE scripts into SEPARATE artifacts and joined at build time with the source recorded per side. That is what makes 'never summed into one grounding number' structural rather than a promise.

Every claim this run inherited from another agent was verified before it was accepted. The 171 correction came from the concurrent run; it was re-measured against news.zip here, and the 10 dropped names were each checked for a page and a floor verdict, before a single number was changed.

Both runs' cross-check selections are DETERMINISTIC - evenly spaced through each context's sorted ingested list, no seed and no shuffle - so the agreement count is a measurement rather than a draw. Re-running after the 171 fix changed the cop pool from 158 to 168 and therefore changed which twenty were picked; the label agreement moved 89.9% -> 88.0% on the new sample and both sit inside I0's measured band.

for_ruling.question: Two completed runs of leg I1 exist in one worktree. Which is canonical, and what sits at harness/notes/ingest/h22_node_corpus.json and harness/notes/receipts/I1.json? They are not mergeable by an agent without a value judgement about whose method wins.
for_ruling.recommendation: Neither dominates and both should be kept until merged deliberately. The concurrent run found the 171 (I1-F1) and this run did not; this run found the declared-version binding defect (I1-F3, worth +99 live parameter matches, still present in theirs) and the parameterless-node classification (I1-F4, which turns 'three of the new COPs need a probe' into 'none do') and that run did not. They agree on 660 of 660 floor verdicts with zero disagreements, which is the strongest evidence either can offer and exists only because both survived. Merge the two corrections into one corpus; do not pick a winner by discarding a run.

for_ruling.question: docs/H22_FRONTIER.md, harness/SYNAPSE_INGEST.md, harness/prompts/i1.md and I0's Q3 all state 161 new Copernicus nodes. Measured: 171. All four are deny-listed from agent edit. Should they be amended?
for_ruling.recommendation: Yes, and amended in place with the evidence rather than silently corrected - the same treatment R86 gave R72's character counts. The corrected statement is stronger, not weaker: 'the shipped what's-new names 171 new Copernicus nodes; SYNAPSE now grounds 168 of them to a stated floor, from a file that ships with the product.' Note also that I0's Q3 reported two independent sources agreeing at exactly 161 with zero set difference - they agreed because both applied the same leading-slash assumption, so source agreement did not detect it. That is worth recording as a method warning, not just a number fix.

for_ruling.question: This leg's POSITIVE control asserted the brief's figure and therefore passed green while the extractor undercounted by 10 (I1-F2). I0's controls had the identical blind spot. Should the harness require that a control's expected value be traceable to a measurement rather than to a governing document?
for_ruling.recommendation: Yes, and it is cheap to enforce: a control whose expectation comes from a document under test must be paired with a BLIND control that reproduces the alternative reading. B8 is the worked example - it shows the slash-only pattern returning 161 - and it costs four lines. Law 1 says every check must be able to fail; this is the corollary it does not currently state, which is that a check must also be able to fail FOR THE RIGHT REASON. A perfectly falsifiable control pinned to an inherited number is a decoration with a green light on it.

for_ruling.question: Should the two runs' known-thin numbers be reported as one integer? This run measures 33 thin pages of which 23 are parameterless nodes and only 10 are real documentation gaps.
for_ruling.recommendation: Report both, labelled, and never merge them. 'Thin' and 'the node has nothing to document' mean opposite things to an artist and to a coverage figure: Copernicus reads as having 13 gaps under the raw floor and ZERO under the classified one, and the second is the true statement. This is the same discipline R72 requires for deprecation - two sources, recorded per side - applied to the floor. It is a product call about what SYNAPSE tells a user, so it is a ruling item.

for_ruling.question: Article V has now been violated twice in two days (H6 on 2026-07-26, I1 today) by the same mechanism: a dispatcher launching a leg into a worktree that already carries a run. Should the launch path carry a structural guard?
for_ruling.recommendation: Yes. A launch guard that refuses to start a leg whose worktree holds an unfinished run - or whose .claude/.orch_launched marker is younger than the leg's last commit - would have prevented both. Article I's corollary already states the principle: enforcement belongs in the definition, not the instruction. Both incidents cost real work: H6 had two competing implementations of the same function silently shadowing each other, and today a completed corpus was destroyed on disk and survived only because a producer path existed to rebuild it. Telling agents to be careful has failed twice; the third time should not be tried.

for_ruling.question: The corpus is built and NOT wired. 660 entries and 12,582 parameter records are one knowledge_lookup away from the surface where U.6 found 15 phantom createNode sites already re-teaching phantoms. What gate must exist before any of this reaches RAG or the emission path?
for_ruling.recommendation: At minimum, the gate must be able to REFUSE an entry, and the per-entry live_label_match field is what makes that possible: 1,739 of the 12,582 documented parameters do NOT resolve to a live parameter label on this build, and those are exactly the records that would teach a phantom. A wiring gate that admits only live-resolved records, tiers the rest as doc-only, and re-runs the resolution on every Houdini build is the shape - but choosing the admission threshold is a product decision with a real recall cost, not an agent call. Out of scope for this leg by standing rule, and named here so the next leg starts from the measurement rather than from zero.

what_the_leg_proves_about_its_own_premis: The brief's premise was that a corpus keyed on the wrong field does not fail loudly - it silently matches nothing - and that this is why I1 had to be gated on I0. Both halves held, and the leg demonstrated them on ITSELF three times rather than on the archive. It bound ten Solaris pages to the wrong live type while every count looked healthy, and only a falsifiable prediction about the live-label rate caught it. It shipped a POSITIVE control that asserted the brief's own figure and therefore passed green while undercounting the flagship surface by ten node types - the failure the brief describes, executed by the instrument built to prevent it. And it lost its finished corpus to a concurrent agent and got it back only because Law 2 had forced a producer path into existence. The most useful thing this leg produced is not the 91.1%; it is that three independent things went wrong quietly and each was caught by a mechanism the constitution already required - a probe, a control, a producer path - rather than by anything looking obviously broken.
